editorial.headline: Specialist Practice: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Independent specialist medical practice is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali records this activity as closed to PMA registration.
editorial.body:
At its core, this classification concerns independent specialist medical practice: the care and treatment of diseases requiring specialist attention. Its stated field includes eye care, ear-nose-throat care, internal medicine, and skin and venereal disease services, when delivered independently by a specialist doctor. That framing matters. This is not a loose label for health services generally; it describes the professional provision of specialised care and treatment by the specialist practitioner. For anyone considering the activity, the practical starting point is therefore the work itself: an independently delivered practice focused on particular diseases and specialty fields.

The registration base is broad in business scale. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises, so no single business size is presented as the only home for the practice. Scale, however, should not be confused with ownership or location. The listed enterprise categories show where the activity may sit by scale; they do not remove the separate PMA position that applies in Bali. Those questions—business scale and foreign-investment access—need to be read independently.

Nationally, the activity is marked TERBUKA for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national position permits full foreign ownership. That is a clear ownership setting, supported in the record by Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. It establishes the national baseline, but it is not the whole answer for a specialist considering a Bali registration.

Bali is where the conclusion changes decisively. The record marks this activity TERTUTUP and states that a foreign specialist cannot open a solo practice under Indonesian health law. For a foreigner, the honest lede is simple: this activity cannot be registered in Bali today. That does not contradict the national 100% ceiling. The national position is open to full foreign ownership, while the Bali record imposes a specific local registration closure. Its stated support also cites a permanent, island-wide provincial PMA moratorium. Nationally open does not mean automatically open in Bali; for this activity, Bali’s closed status determines the Bali registration outcome.
